Name: Rage Engine
Description:
NEW IN 0.25:
- Syringes now in the item book: Serums, Super Serums, Serum Vials, Custom Serums.
- Throw NPCs: yank hard, lift them, or grab with both hands and pull (judo).
- NPCs walk around bodies and don't break bones tripping over things.
- They keep their weapons more; heads smash easier, especially on the floor.
- Fist fights: punches from real boxing motion capture, closer and more aggressive, real blocking.
- Toxin oils: touch a bottle to your blade to coat it.
- Serum Lab (Mod Options): combine serums, super serums and toxins into your own, with combination reactions.
- New gore: broken noses, teeth knocked out, throat cuts with arterial spurts, blades pulled from the gut, eye gouging.
- Real recorded sounds only; NPC voices are the game's own.

NEW IN 0.24: Serums and super serums: modelled syringes, injectors and vials; 6 serums, 9 super serums with glowing eyes and auras.

NEW IN 0.23:
- TOXINS: 7 coated daggers in the item book (category "Rage Engine Toxins") and Mod Options buttons to coat whatever weapon you hold. Neurotoxin (purple skin, choking, suffocation), Paralytic (arms then legs go dead), Hemotoxin (bleeding from everywhere), Sedative (falls asleep), Acid (spreading burns), Berserk (rage serum, then a crash), Terror (drops everything and runs). Coated tips drip. "Toxins can kill" in Deaths.
- Higher-HP NPCs are tougher: more pain tolerance, stronger grip, steadier, slower to poison.
- Easier to grab: a held NPC goes looser and stops getting pushed around by other systems - much less bouncing.
- Punch-drunk is calmer: smaller sway, fewer lurches.
- Red Room Diner map ships inside this mod folder.

NEW IN 0.22:
- FIXED: NPCs getting dragged to the middle of the map / arm stuck there with 3+ NPCs. An IK safety watchdog frees any hand pinned to a stale or far-away anchor, recycled bodies are cleaned, and the 'come here' wave lets go of the hand.
- PRESSURE POINTS (Mod Options > Rage Engine: Pressure Points): critical injury zones (upper/lower torso, abdomen, neck, shoulders, arms, legs) with Mild/Severe/Extreme severity, Temporary/Encounter/Persistent injuries and smooth sink-to-the-ground transitions.
- Injuries finally work together: a broken leg + a broken arm, both legs, a ruined torso - the body gives out. Critical NPCs know it: they stop fighting, try to get away, wheeze and gasp.
- 42 new wound textures: lacerations, stab wounds, bullet entry/exit, split skin, crush wounds, open fractures, scrapes, skull fractures, blood drips, splatter, pools on the ground.
- Bruises go through stages - contusion, deep contusion, hematoma (the skin really swells), split skin.
- Skulls crack before they smash; a hard hammer blow (or slow motion) can smash one: skull fragments, brain, teeth. New Deaths options: Head smashing on/off and Head smash ease.
- New bones: ribs, hand bones, vertebrae, jaw fragments.
- No more snap-back after hard hits; running trips never break legs; NPCs catch their balance on the run.
- Better blocking: skill-based guard against head AND body punches, armed NPCs block with their free hand, and the game's own parrying is tuned per NPC (and gets worse as they get hurt or punch-drunk).

NEW IN 0.21 (polish from your playtest):
- New "Rage Engine: Deaths" settings: Shock can kill, Bleeding out can kill, Knockouts can kill, Choke-outs can kill - turn them off for boss fights.
- Knockouts with "can kill" off: they come round after 6-12 s, groggy and punch-drunk, and fight on.
- Pain tolerance: a light poke no longer makes NPCs drop everything. Dropping a weapon from pain now takes real pain from a real hit.
- Fist fighters don't surrender after one punch: an NPC who squared up only quits when he's badly hurt.
- Punch-drunk: head shots stack up - confused face, lolling head, swaying, lurching steps they catch, late swings, groans. Sobers up over about a minute; a drunk NPC is easier to knock out.
- Steadier on their feet: NPCs pull themselves back upright after a hit, stumble less, and hurt legs bend instead of folding.
- Pistol fits your hand: barrel along your hand, grip in your palm, and it shoots where the barrel points. Bat and pipe models line up with the weapon you actually swing.

NEW IN 0.20:
- FIXED: NPCs spawning with the invisible fist tool, getting their arm stuck at the middle of the map and dying. Fists only go on after 8 s, only if they truly have no weapon, and a watchdog drops anything that drifts away from a hand.
- No weapon theft: NPCs can't pull weapons out of your hands or out of their own wounds-on-you; weapons they hold can't be yanked by the game's disarm.
- Lightning: Rage Engine steps back completely while an NPC is electrocuted, so the game's shock animation plays clean.
- NPC health is now an absolute 0-5000 HP slider.
- Toys (Mod Options > Rage Engine: Toys): modelled pistol, dynamite bundle, baseball bat and lead pipe.
- Back hits arch them forward and they reach for the spot; leg damage buckles and bows the knee instead of dropping or ignoring it.
- Knockouts: enough head trauma and they go limp, eyes shut, then die (counts as dead for waves).
- Big chest slashes make them drop the weapon and stop fighting. Hands can break. Rib shots make them cough blood. Every bone break gets a scream and a shock reaction.
- Impaled NPCs grab the weapon and pull it out, or wince.
- Fists: when they lose their weapon they shout a challenge and square up; some fair fighters drop their weapon and beckon you if you're barehanded.
- Thrown NPCs who are angry enough get up and charge you.
- Groups: only two attack at once; the rest circle and flank.
- Faces: pain, fear, anger, confusion and exhaustion show on their faces.
- Surprise 1: Rage Moments - a skull crush, spine snap or knockout drops time into slow motion for a heartbeat.
- Surprise 2: Old scars - named NPCs who escaped you come back carrying the scars and the limp you gave them.
- Gore craters replaced by red flesh chunks and painted wounds.

NEW IN 0.12 (built from your playtest log):
- Fixed NPCs dropping after 2-3 punches: Rage Engine was weakening the trunk muscles of hurt, coughing or wincing NPCs, and B&S's balance-driven ragdoll fell over. The trunk and legs now keep full strength while standing, and a knockdown guard keeps them up if the game tries to drop them from an ordinary hit.
- New hit physics: a real impulse at the exact contact point (heads snap and twist, chests rock) plus the game's own stagger step on solid hits.
- Fist fighting that works: the game makes disarmed NPCs run away, so Rage Engine gives them an invisible phantom weapon. They square up, jab, swing and block with the game's real melee animations, and their fists do damage to you.
- 141 new real recorded sounds: punches, body hits, stabs, bullet impacts, bone cracks, male and female pain and death screams. Credits are in SOUND_CREDITS.md.
- Textures shipped as files (Textures folder), plus a 'Gore material' option to switch how gore is drawn in-game.
- Gore only from genuinely huge impacts; no more bone shards in heads, hands or feet.

NEW IN 0.11 (stability overhaul):
- Grounded: the game's own hit reactions are retuned on every NPC's brain at runtime, so ordinary hits don't throw them on the floor. Legs are never loosened while standing, and hurt legs limp instead of buckling, which ends the random tripping.
- Clean NPCs: everything Rage Engine changes on a body (eyes, jaw, crushed head, joints) is put back when the game re-uses it, which fixes the deformed faces on new spawns.
- Realistic bones: one very heavy blunt hit, or repeated heavy hits on the same limb, breaks a bone; ordinary punches never do. Bone sticks out only on severe breaks.
- Textured gore: textured bone, flesh chunks in the NPC's own skin colour, torn wound craters and blotchy bruises. Chunks can't trip anyone.
- Fisticuffs: disarmed NPCs put their fists up, snatch nearby weapons, throw plates, bowls and bottles at you, and cover up when you swing.
- Decapitation is always instant (no headless revives).
- Compatible with Realistic Deaths (detected automatically) and RealisticBlood. Rage Engine no longer replaces any game brains or creatures.
- Waves: Civilians (endless) and Duel (endless).

PHYSICAL STATE - every NPC tracks balance, posture (steady/unsteady/stumbling/down/getting up/shaky), pain, fatigue, toughness and limb condition; movement, reflexes and recovery all follow it.

HIT REACTIONS - real physics from contact (mass x speed): thrown objects, pokes, punches, kicks, bashes. The hit spot goes loose and is shoved: head snaps, gut folds, shoulder twists, leg gives. Balance drains with each hit. Escalates through flinch, stagger, full stagger, dazed (head), knee buckle (legs), fall with a real tumble.

GROUNDED - feet stay planted; small hits are pure physics (no canned staggers), heavy hits make them step to catch themselves, only a genuinely heavy force (big thrown object, explosion) knocks anyone down, and they get up fast. Player punches are human-strength.

TOUGHNESS - most NPCs take a punch and stay on their feet; one ordinary hit never drops a composed NPC. Once they're reeling, follow-ups put them down. About 1 in 8 has a glass jaw and goes flying.

REFLEXES - arms swing out to catch their balance; next to a wall they brace a hand on it.

FALLS - hurt NPCs stay down longer, writhe and hold wounds; everyone gets up differently and is shaky afterwards; hard hits can knock weapons from their hands.

BONES (blunt only) - arms, legs and jaws break with a snap, crunch, controller buzz and a scream. Broken arms drop the weapon and dangle on physics; broken legs buckle, then limp; broken jaws hang crooked. Open fractures show bone through the skin and bleed.

RIBS - hard body blows wind them (they double over and hold it) and can crack ribs; cracked ribs hurt with every breath.

VISIBLE DAMAGE & SHOCK - they hunch, wince and slow as they're hurt; set NPC health up to 10x for long fights; long critical pain or blood loss sends them into shock and they die.

BRUISING - blunt hits bruise where they land (face too): red, then purple, then dark purple; repeat hits make them bigger and darker.

WOUNDS - cut hands and arms get a weak, trembling grip but they fight on; badly cut arms go dead and the weapon switches to the good hand; NPCs press hands on bleeding chest and neck wounds and keep going back to them; leg cuts drop them, then they limp; forehead cuts put blood in their eyes and they wipe it; pokes get a reaction.

BLEEDING - deep stabs, open fractures and stumps drain health; blood in the airway makes them cough blood.

DISMEMBERMENT - they survive losing a limb, scream and hold the stump (bone visible); most keep fighting, some flee; losing a leg keeps them on the ground.

DYING MOMENTS - a fatal blow lets them finish their swing, reel and stumble as their strength drains, then collapse in the direction of the blow.

ADRENALINE - some 'killed' NPCs fight on for a few seconds, screaming, before dropping.

CHOKING - grab the neck: red eyes, choking and gurgling, controller vibration that fades as they go limp; they pass out (or die, your choice).

PERSONALITIES - calm, confident, nervous, aggressive, cautious or unpredictable; witnesses get shaken and may panic.

TEST TOOLS - spawn a test pistol and dynamite from Mod Options to try the physics.

SOUNDS - 41 public-domain sound effects: punches, body hits and falls, bone and rib cracks, flesh slashes and stabs, dismemberment, gunshots, explosions.

Works with RealisticBlood and with death-animation mods (turn off Dying moments if you prefer theirs).
Author: Rage Engine
